Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – JULY 7, 2022

A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on July 7, 2022, via
Zoom. Commissioner Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

Present
  Commissioner Henry Brown, Commissioner at Large
  Commissioner Lee Denmon, District One
  Commissioner Cynthia, McLemore, District Three
  Commissioner Christopher Beck, District Four
  Thomas Uwal, Human Services Superintendent
  Juan Mata, Parks Supervisor
  Anthony Harris, Recreation Supervisor
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent
  Commissioner Jacob Fragoso, District Two
  Sabrina Barnes, Director-Parks, Recreation, and Community Services

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Brown made the motion to approve the minutes from June 2, 2022.
Commissioner McLemore seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Brown, McLemore, and Denmon
  Nays: None

Staff Report

  Stephanie Maldonado presented a staff report recommending the Park and Recreation
Commission recommend the Mayor and Council Members adopt a resolution accepting a donation
in the amount of $65,000 from the American Heart Association for Greenfield fitness stations for
Rogers Park.

  Commissioner McLemore made a motion to approve the staff report and Commissioner
Brown seconded. The motion was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Brown, McLemore, and Denmon
  Nays: None

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – JULY 7, 2022

  Stephanie Maldonado presented a staff report recommending the Park and Recreation
Commission recommend the Mayor and Council Members take the following actions:
  a. Award the Darby Park Restroom Project Phase 1 (CB-22-03) to Doja, Inc.;
  b. Approve an agreement with Doja, Inc. in the amount of $630,000; and
  c. Approve a contingency amount of $63,000.00 for a total cost of $693,000 (General Fund)

  Commissioner Denmon asked if this was the new bid. Thomas Uwal stated yes, it was a
rebid and Doja, Inc. was the lowest bidder and has met all the city’s requirements.

  Commissioner Brown made a motion to approve the staff report and Commissioner Denmon
seconded. The motion was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Brown, McLemore, and Denmon
  Nays: None

Verbal Reports

  Juan Mata gave a verbal report on behalf of the Parks Administration regarding the following:
   Park staff replaced a 3-inch irrigation backflow at North Park
   The splash pad at Ashwood Park is open and is being heavily used by kids.
  Operating hours are from 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
   The Graffiti Abatement staff has been busy in District 2 and District 3 including
  Rogers Park, the exterior of the restroom, skate area, and snack bar container. Also
  on Florence Avenue traveling south of Eucalyptus into the residential area has
  heavily tagged.

  Commissioner Denmon asked when the splash pad was reopened. Mr. Mata stated on June
27, 2022.

  Anthony Harris gave a verbal report on behalf of the Recreation Division regarding the
following:
   Summer Day Camp: We are excited to report our Summer Day Camps at Darby,
  Rogers and Siminski Parks are going extremely well. We have a total of 200 youth
  ages 3-12 enrolled in each session. Camp is packed with excitement, enrichment,
  and fun. Campers enjoy a different theme each session as well as participate in
  enrichment programming, specialty activities, social recreation, and field trips. The
  kids are having a blast creating memories that will last a lifetime!
   Dodgers Dream team: The Dodgers Dream team program in the City of Inglewood
  served 175 youth ages 5-8 in the Spring Season. The current Summer Season is
  loaded with 20 baseball and softball teams totaling 279 participants between the
  ages of 11 – 18. This season brings a complete in-house league that includes a
  four-team Senior Softball Division for the very first time. The Senior Softball Division

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – JULY 7, 2022
  includes high school team participation from Animo Charter and Morningside High
  Schools. In addition, multiple softball teams are being led by volunteer coaches from
  the Natasha Watley Foundation. The Junior Softball Division pits two teams against
  each other weekly. Every game is a championship game and in the last three weeks,
  both teams have alternated winning by one run. We are proud of the increasing
  number of female participants in this program (86 current female participants, 156
  total) and look to build off of the momentum into other sports offerings. Another
  aspect to mention is our Umpire Training program here in the city which was
  implemented this year, produced 6 promising umpires, and has allowed the league
  to run efficiently. The "Summer Season" playoffs begin on August 12 th and conclude
  with our Championship weekend on August 20th. We will celebrate our youth
  immediately following games on August 20 th which includes food, fun, and awards
  for all participants.
    The Edward Vincent, Jr. Park Swim complex officially opened on Wednesday, June
  22, 2022. The first session of Youth Swim Lessons began on June 22, 2022, with
  over 100 students enrolled. Adult Swim, Parent and Me swim classes will begin on
  July 9, 2022, Lap Swim begins July 6, 2022, and general swim is offered
  Wednesday through Sunday from 1:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. Admission is $1 per
  person. We invite the entire community to join us for Family Swim Nights on
  Wednesday evenings from 5:30 p.m. to 7:00 p.m.
    Movies in the Park: We are extremely excited about the return of Movies in the Park.
  Join us on Saturday, July 16, 2022, at Inglewood City Hall (Disney/Pixar's "Luca")
  and Saturday, August 13, 2022, at North Park (Walt Disney Animations Studios
  "Encanto"). All movies are free and began at dusk. Food and refreshments will be
  available for purchase. Bring 10 recyclable items and receive a free popcorn
  voucher. For additional information, contact the Parks, Recreation and Community
  Services Department.

  Commissioner Brown *inaudible.

  Commissioner Denmon inquired about a rodeo event scheduled at Edward Vincent Park.
Mr. Harris gave the date, location, and a slight overview of the event.

  Commissioner Beck both commended and applauded Mr. Harris for all the hard work he
was doing and also thanked him.

  Thomas Uwal gave a verbal report on behalf of the Human Services Division regarding the
following:
   Nutrition: We are serving approximately 350 seniors per week and continue to
  provide LA Food Bank boxes monthly and fresh produce weekly. Our Nutrition staff
  including our Home Delivery Meals staff continue to be dedicated to serving and
  delivering our seniors their daily meals. Our dining room is closed for congregate
  dining due to COVID and there is no projected opening date yet.
  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – JULY 7, 2022
    Summer Food: Our summer food program started on June 13, 2022. We are serving
  at seven different locations to youth 18 and under. The sites are Ashwood Park,
  Crenshaw Library, Darby Park, Siminiski Park, Lock heaven Community Center,
  Rogers Park, and Edward Jr. Vincent Park. We are providing breakfast, lunch, and
  snacks at different sites and the times will vary according to the sites.
    CACFP Program: The Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) was successful
  and our audit was completed with no findings. The program provided Grab-N-Go
  meals to youth 18 and younger at three sites (Crenshaw Library, Rogers Park, and
  Darby Park).
    Transportation: Our Senior and Disabled Paratransit service continues to provide
  trips to critical appointments such as dialysis and doctors' appointments. Drivers, as
  well as passengers, continue to wear facemasks coverings. We have also been
  scheduling seniors and persons with disabilities to other next-day requested
  appointments, and if resources are available, same-day service requests may be
  serviced as well. Beginning, July 1, the City of Inglewood no longer provides
  paratransit services to the City of Lennox. A new service provider has since taken
  over. The transition from one service agency to the other (MV Transit Div. 14) went
  seamless with no issues that we are currently aware of. Drivers have completed,
  refresher driver safety training, which focused on topics related to distracted
  driving. Drivers found the training to be informative, which helps them to stay aware
  and abreast of safe driving techniques to utilize while operating city vehicles.
    Senior Center Operations: Since the partial opening of the Inglewood Senior Center,
  we have been able to add a few more activities such as chess, bridge, and line
  dancing. Seniors are still expected to wear face coverings, have their temperatures
  checked, practice safe distancing as well as provide proof of their full vaccination.
  These measures are required to enter and participate in activities. These measures
  will continue until further notice so we can ensure our seniors are as safe as
  possible.

  Commissioner Beck asked will food delivery continue for seniors in the city of Hawthorne or
will that be tabled along with Lennox. Mr. Uwal stated we are under a current contract with
Hawthorne, there will be no change. Commissioner Beck expressed how important our seniors are
and acknowledged Human Services dedication to serving our seniors.

  Commissioner Brown inquired about a transportation schedule. Mr. Uwal gave an overview
of the types of transportation the department offers.

  4
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – JULY 7, 2022
Director’s Report

  Thomas Uwal gave a verbal report regarding the Dodgers Dream Field Letter of intent:
   The Parks, Recreation, and Community Services Department has received a letter
  of intent from the Los Angeles Dodgers Foundation (LADF) to partner with the city
  to build two Dodgers Dream Fields at Edward Vincent Park. The project will include
  the installation of new fencing, scoreboard, and irrigation. The plan is to start
  construction in September of 2022 with an expected unveiling event following in
  April or May 2023. The project's budget is estimated at one million dollars, with major
  funding from the Los Angeles Dodgers, Security Benefit, Nike, and more. A final
  agreement will be presented to the Mayor and City Council by August 2022.

  Commissioner Beck asked which park this will take place. Mr. Uwal replied Edward Vincent
Park. Commissioner Denmon asked if the irrigation plan was separate from an already emplaced
plan. Mr. Harris stated he believes it's only for the ball diamonds. Juan Mata stated that irrigation is
a separate contract. Commissioner Beck stated this is exciting news and commended the Dodgers
for their investment.

Public Comments

  None

Commissioner’s Comments

  Commissioner Brown gave a brief explanation about his attendance and asked about the
MLK Event planning. Stephanie Maldonado stated she’d check with Director Barnes and follow up
with an email.

With no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 6:31 p.m.

  5
